item.title: NASA launches its Roman Space Telescope to explore the hidden universe
item.description: NASA's Roman Space Telescope​ launched shortly after daybreak from Kennedy Space Center and blazed toward an observation point 1 million miles away.

item.title: Grand Canyon flash floods leave more than 20 missing, dozens evacuated
item.description: The flash floods hit Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area on Saturday afternoon, the National Park Service said.

item.title: U.S. military strikes Iranian targets in first military action in a month
item.description: As the war passes the six-month mark, neither side showed any sign of backing down.

item.title: Ross Fire burns 85,000 acres, leaves destruction across 2 counties
item.description: The Ross wildfire has burned more than 80,000 acres across Palo Pinto and Jack counties, forcing evacuations, closing roads and disrupting schools.

item.title: Nicolás Maduro shares photos from New York prison: "We are standing firm"
item.description: In the two photographs, Venezuela's deposed leader Nicolás Maduro is wearing a gray tracksuit and making peace signs with his hands.

item.title: Former Afghan general says chaos at Kabul airport was "the worst situation of my life"
item.description: As the world marks five years since the U.S. troop withdrawal from Afghanistan, former Afghan General Haibatullah Alizai tells "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that as he looks back at the chaotic withdrawal, it is the "worst situation of my life," adding that he was thinking of the families of his friends who were killed and "I didn't have any answers for their families at that point."

item.title: Google updates maps to show "Lake America" in U.S. after Trump order
item.description: Google announced that it had begun rolling out changes to how its maps display Lake Ontario's name, after President Trump signed an executive order changing it to "Lake America."

item.description: On this "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" broadcast, Sen. Richard Blumenthal and Rep. John James join Margaret Brennan.

item.title: At least 1 killed, 5 injured in shooting at rave in Switzerland
item.description: Local police said early Sunday a manhunt was underway and the motives were still unclear.

item.title: NASA's groundbreaking Roman Space Telescope launches into space
item.description: Using a donated Hubble-class mirror originally built for a spy satellite, NASA's Roman Space Telescope launched Sunday on a $4.3 billion mission to open a new window on the universe, taking wide-angle, ultra-sharp images that would require a half million 4K TVs to show in full.

item.title: Blumenthal urges House to pass Russia sanctions amid "extreme urgency" in Ukraine
item.description: Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut urged the House to approve the Senate-passed Russia sanctions bill amid a "moment of extreme urgency" in the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Indianapolis Colts player Keenan Allen arrested on drunken driving charges
item.description: Keenan Allen, a longtime NFL player who recently signed with the Indianapolis Colts, was arrested early Sunday for operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated, police said.

item.title: FBI revises hiring standards regarding prostitution, stealing from employer
item.description: The FBI has revised its hiring standards and no longer disqualifies applicants who admitted to hiring prostitutes or stealing from an employer. The new guidelines come following the retirement, resignation and termination of scores of FBI agents during the second Trump administration.

item.title: Face the Nation: Becker, Alizai
item.description: Missed the second half of the show? CBS election analyst David Becker and former Afghan General Haibatullah Alizai join Margaret Brennan.

item.title: USS Lincoln sails past Singapore after 9-month deployment
item.description: Associated Press journalists on the Indonesian island of Batam, across the Singapore Strait, spotted the massive vessel as it transited waters near Singapore just after 1 a.m. local time.

item.title: David Becker says there is "no time" for Trump executive order on mail voting to be implemented
item.description: CBS News election analyst David Becker told "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that there is "simply no time" to put in place President Trump's executive order restricting mail voting. "I think for 2026, this is almost certainly not going to be implemented," Becker said.

item.title: 3 NBC journalists, Palestinian woman attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
item.description: Three journalists from NBC and a Palestinian woman they were interviewing were attacked by Israeli settlers in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Saturday. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu swiftly condemned the attackers, referring to them as "rioters" and called for an investigation.

item.title: John James, GOP governor candidate, says tariffs can't "be borne on the backs of Michiganders"
item.description: Amid the trade war between Canada and the U.S. that will likely affect Michigan and the auto industry, Rep. John James, the Republican candidate for governor in Michigan, told "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that he has been in contact with members of the trade team because "it cannot be borne on the backs of Michiganders."

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Aug. 30): "By Design"
item.description: "Sunday Morning" presents its annual edition touching on all aspects of design, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: 2 dead, 8 wounded in Trenton shooting, prosecutor says
item.description: Two people died and eight others were hurt in a shooting on Locust Street in Trenton early Sunday morning, officials say.

item.title: Sen. Blumenthal urges House to pass Russia sanctions bill amid "moment of extreme urgency"
item.description: Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut, who recently returned from a trip to the Ukraine region, told "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that the House must forward on the Russia sanctions bill that has already passed the Senate. "It is a moment of extreme urgency," he added.

item.title: 8/30: Face The Nation
item.description: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Sen. Richard Blumenthal, who is recently back from the Ukraine region, joins to discuss the latest. Plus, with five years having passed since the U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan, a former Afghan general shares his story of the dramatic flight from the country.

item.title: The one and only Dolly Parton: A tribute
item.description: "Sunday Morning" looks back at the astonishing career of the queen of country music, whose talent, warmth, wit, and philanthropy made her a genuine, once-in-a-generation luminary.

item.title: Philadelphia architect Frank Furness' enduring spirit
item.description: Philadelphia architect Frank Furness, a former Army captain during the Civil War, translated his fearlessness into the designs of about 1,000 buildings – elaborate structures whose oversized arches, asymmetrical facades and eccentric decorations broke free from the polite Victorian era-style. "Sunday Morning" national correspondent Robert Costa takes a tour of Furness' Philadelphia with Wall Street Journal architectural critic Michael Lewis, who explains why the architect's reputation has gained a reappraisal. [Original air date: May 17, 2026.]

item.title: 8/30: Sunday Morning
item.description: Jane Pauley hosts our annual look at design. Featured: Tiny homes in your backyard; Louis Vuitton; Adobe house construction; Finland's Marimekko; domino art; Philadelphia food favorites; chandeliers; Longwood Gardens; and rare maps. Also: A tribute to Dolly Parton.

item.title: Nepal flash flood death toll reaches 800, with around 3,000 still missing
item.description: Poor weather and challenging terrain have hampered aerial rescue operations in Nepal and Tibet.

item.title: Trump cannot deport students for criticizing Israel, federal judge rules
item.description: The judge delivered a victory for Stanford University's student newspaper, which said some international students were afraid to speak out because of the deportation threat.

item.title: Ontario premier slams Trump's order: "It's Lake Ontario now and forever"
item.description: Amid an ongoing trade war​ between Canada and the United States, President Trump last week sought to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America" by executive order.
